findings.reason: The protected source is already expert-level interview code. `hostname`, `visited`, `pending`, `completed`, `future`, and `neighbor` expose the host boundary and future lifecycle directly. A fixed `ThreadPoolExecutor` overlaps blocking parser calls, `FIRST_COMPLETED` avoids level barriers, and one coordinator owns both mutable sets, so locks and race-prone shared worker state are unnecessary. No candidate would materially improve correctness, asymptotic complexity, clarity, naming, or resource discipline.

The start URL is marked before its first fetch. The coordinator accepts a neighbor only when its extracted hostname exactly matches the fixed starting hostname and it is not already visited, then marks it before submission. Thus every scheduled URL is a reachable same-host page fetched once. Conversely, every scheduled page has all outgoing links inspected; induction along a valid reachability path proves completeness. The pending set becomes empty only after every scheduled fetch is consumed, so completion is independent of worker finish order.

Only executor workers call the injected blocking parser; only the coordinator reads or mutates `visited` and `pending`. This eliminates check-then-schedule races without a lock, bounds active parser calls to eight, submits work as soon as any fetch finishes, handles cycles and converging frontiers, and propagates worker exceptions through `future.result()` instead of silently returning an incomplete crawl.
